instantiated_cells.justification: Principals/clients file semi-annual reports due July 15 and January 15, not annual reports.
The statute specifies semi-annual filing dates for client reports and does not require monthly principal spending reports.
Client spending reports are expressly semi-annual, so no other frequency option is specified for principals in this section.
No quarterly reporting requirement is imposed on clients; instead the statute requires semi-annual reports.
Clients meeting the threshold must file 'semi-annual reports' by July 15 and January 15.
The statute does not provide for tri-annual (legislative-calendar-linked) principal reporting.
The semi-annual report contents list identifying information, lobbyists, issues, expenditures, and business relationships, but not the client's business nature (public vs private).
The client must report 'the compensation paid or owed to each such lobbyist'.
Clients must disclose the subject matters/bill numbers and the person or body before which they lobbied, but the statute does not require reporting individual lobbying contacts/communications.
The report must include 'a description of the general subject or subjects' lobbied.

Clients must report 'any other expenses paid or incurred ... for the purpose of lobbying' with itemization rules, which encompasses non-compensation costs such as entertainment, travel, etc., except for specified exclusions.
Beyond lobbyist compensation, the client must disclose 'any other expenses paid or incurred ... for the purpose of lobbying' (i.e., non-compensation/indirect costs) subject to exclusions.
The report must list 'the name, address and telephone number of each lobbyist retained, employed or designated by such client'.
Clients must disclose each lobbyist they retain, employ, or designate.
Certain clients (meeting spending and percentage thresholds) must report sources of funding over $5,000 used to fund the lobbying activities.
The semi-annual report must contain the client's 'name, address and telephone number'.
The report must include 'the legislative bill numbers of any bills' lobbied.
Clients must disclose compensation paid/owed to lobbyists plus other lobbying expenses, together constituting total lobbying expenditures reported by the principal.
The statute requires client spending reports to include the specific 'compensation paid or owed to each such lobbyist' (salary/fees).
Expenses must be aggregated only if $75 or less; if more than $75 they must be detailed as to amount, payee, and purpose (itemization).
No provision in the semi-annual client report requires associations to list all sponsors or members.

Clients must list each lobbyist retained, employed or designated, but the statute does not separately require identifying individual in-house employees/lobbyists employed by the client beyond those lobbyists.
